817) Thus, because the Śiva-liṅga is the locus for the entry of all sounds (*dhvani*), it is said to be of the nature of dissolution (*layātmaka*). Now, in the Siddhānta...

To indicate that these [deities] are of the same nature as those whose abode is *tarasamaya* (the power of speed), by virtue of being a part of this [same category], he states their stationing within the lower principles: "The forms of Viṣṇu’s partial incarnations (*daśāvatāra*) abide in the principle of earth (*pṛthvī-tattva*)."

The forms of the ten incarnations (daśāvatāra-mūrtayaḥ) are specific manifestations of the first incarnation (matsyādyavatāra-mūrti-bhedāḥ). They abide in the element of earth (pṛthvī-tattve sthitāḥ). [They are] within the sphere of the elements, the heart, the intellect, the ego, the secondary self (gauṇa-puṃs), the Lords of Knowledge (vidyeśvara), and the individual soul (gocaraḥ).
These are the twelve [deities] beginning with Mitra, the twelve beginning with Keśava, and the twelve beginning with Tryambaka; thus the group beginning with Mitra is threefold.
The twelve beginning with Keśava, and the twelve beginning with Tryambaka—thus there are twelve in each of these three groups;

they are situated respectively within the twelve principles, starting from earth: the five elements, mind, the principle of intellect (*buddhi-tattva*), the principle of ego (*ahaṅkāra-tattva*), the qualities (*guṇa*), the principle of the individual soul (*puruṣa-tattva*), the principle of knowledge (*vidyā-tattva*), and the principle of the Lord (*īśvara-tattva*).

This is the meaning. Vighnarāja resides in Sādākhya; likewise, O Goddess Sarasvatī, Nandī and the others reside in Śuddhavidyā; Lakṣmī resides in the sphere of Īśvara; the Jainas are established in Prakṛti; and the Śakyas are situated in Buddhi; [the followers of] Puruṣa [reside] in Puruṣa.
O Śivā, the five classes of beings are established within the two suns:
the *spasara*, yakṣas, rākṣasas, vidyādharas, and kinnaras; as well as bhūtas, vetālas, ḍākinīs, the planets, lunar mansions, and zodiac signs; and the oceans, kṣetrapālas, and so forth.
The sages, Brahmā, and the lords of the directions are to be known as abiding in the principle of *ūrū* (the thighs).

Those born of old age, those born of passion, the egg-born, and the soil-born [are likewise situated there]. Furthermore, for others as well, wherever their respective stations among the principles (*tattva*) may be, they are established therein.

The entire placement (*nyāsa*) ending with the toothless one (*dantamasta*) is that very other non-place; for it is indeed that which serves as the locus for those respective states of the faces beginning with Vighnarāja and ending with the Lords of the Quarters (*digīśvara*) during their installations (*pratiṣṭhā*).
The placement (nyāsa) extending up to each respective reality-level (tattva) must be performed; for those [levels], that very specific location is itself the supreme state (paramapada).

For this very reason, all practitioners of the observances (samayins) consider the very status prescribed by their own respective scriptures to be the highest of all. This being so, even among those various scriptures...
If it is argued that because it was composed by such a Great Being (mahāpuruṣa), the Śaiva scripture might also be tainted by the suspicion of invalidity due to doubt,
[we reply] no, because this [scripture] was indeed composed by Śiva, who is endowed with qualities such as omniscience.
Nor should it be said that even for the Sugata, because he is omniscient,
his own treatise is not an authoritative means of knowledge (*pramāṇa*),
since omniscience is established for Kapila and others as well through the practice of yoga and so forth; for both [the Buddha and Kapila] are alike in this regard.

If it is argued that there is no abandonment of omniscience [on our part], we say no, because of the composition of mutually contradictory treatises. As it has been said: "If Sugata is omniscient, Kapila is not; if both were omniscient, there would be a divergence of opinion."

How so? Therefore, by the mere thorough knowledge of those respective principles (*tattva*), the other [principles] are reduced to being merely that respective principle alone. Since the *Śiva-śāstra* was composed by the omniscient Supreme Śiva, the supreme status belongs exclusively to the principle of Śiva as propounded therein.
And it has already been established previously that initiation alone is the means for attaining that state; likewise, in the Sarvajñānottara (p.
There shall be a single place of liberation, stainless and facing all directions; it is immovable, all-pervading, peaceful, and free from the stages of life (āśramas) and sectarian marks (liṅgas).

Thus, for those who have conquered their own selves, liberation comes through initiation (*dīkṣā*), and they do not perceive those abodes of liberation as "O Six-faced One. Now, in the *Pratiṣṭhā* [kalā], there is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the Form (*mūrti*), the Lord of the Form (*mūrtīśvara*), the Principle (*tatva*), and the Lord of the Principle (*tatveśvara*).
